chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Al-Amraki ibn Ali, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a man who is overtaken by the month of Ramadan while traveling, and he stays for some days in a place; is fasting upon him? He said: No, until he intends to stay for ten days. And if he intends to stay for ten days, he fasts and completes the prayer. I asked him about a man who has outstanding days from the month of Ramadan while he is traveling, and he repays them when he stays in a place; he said: No, until he intends to stay for ten days.
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum duration a traveler must intend to stay to be considered a resident for fasting and prayer purposes in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the Shia jurisprudential criterion for transitioning from traveler status to resident status, requiring an intention to stay for ten days to obligate full fasting and prayer. It specifically addresses the nuance of making up missed Ramadan days while traveling, ruling that one must intend to remain in the location for ten days before the obligation to fast applies. This ruling underscores the importance of intention (niyyah) in determining legal status within Shia fiqh.
